concept.name: Average winner
concept.definition: The mean profit of the winning trades in a sample: total gross profit divided by the number of winning trades. It is one of the two size components (with the average loser) that, combined with the win rate, determine expectancy.
concept.intuition: It measures how big the typical win is — the win leg of the win-size/loss-size asymmetry that makes or breaks a system.
concept.mechanics: Sum the PnL of all trades with positive results (net of costs) and divide by their count. It is reported in currency, percent, or R-multiples for comparability across systems and sizes.
concept.formula: Average winner = gross profit / number of winning trades.
concept.failure_modes: Highly sensitive to outliers: one outsized winner can dominate the mean and mask a mediocre typical win, so medians or trimmed means are often more robust. Backtested average winners shrink when slippage and fees are added.
concept.misconceptions: A large average winner does not guarantee profitability: if winners are rare enough (low win rate), expectancy can still be negative.
concept.example: If 40 winning trades made $12,000 in total, the average winner is $300; against an average loser of $150 the payoff ratio is 2.
